suggestions.title: Lights out by 00:30 tonight — Sunday's 01:40 bed cost you 1.3 hours

rationale.science: At a matched deficit, short sleep (5.5 vs 8.5 h) cut fat loss by about 55% and raised lean-mass loss by about 60% — sleep decides how much of what you lose comes off muscle rather than fat (Nedeltcheva 2010; Wang 2018).
rationale.data: Last four nights 5.0 / 7.0 / 7.0 / 6.17 h against 7.42 / 7.50 / 7.83 the week before — a 2.8 h debt over seven nights against the 7.5 h target you set on 7/28 and held for a week.
rationale.relationship: Your wake time barely moves (07:35–08:00), so bedtime is the whole variable: 00:20 buys 7.0 h, Sunday's 01:40 bought 6.17. Nothing on this card is about caffeine — your caffeine log stops 7/28 and I won't build on a blank.

suggestions.predict: Bed by 00:30 tonight puts you back at 7–7.5 h. Expect the 7-night debt under 2 h by Thursday, and your next leg day — which carries the 155 debut and the 0-RIR bill — to run without a short night sitting in the middle of it.

suggestions.title: Strike Friday's ham curl before you train legs — your note says you skipped it

rationale.science: Progression only protects you if the baseline is real — double progression is measured against reps actually performed (Schoenfeld 2017). An unearned bump is exactly what cratered extension 155 on 7/21 and forced the revert.
rationale.data: Friday's session note reads "Ham curl skipped this sesh for time. Abnormal" while the log shows ham 120 × 12,12 — the only lift that day carrying no effort score at all (rir null), against rir 2 on your real ham entries on 7/24 and 7/28. exercises.ham now reads topAt 120, topRun 1.
rationale.relationship: Your app has already written "repeat it and the load queues itself," and your next session is a leg day — so one real ham session queues 125 off a set you say you never did.

suggestions.predict: Strike the entry (or move it into Friday's skipped list) before you train and topRun resets to 0; ham holds at 120 until you put up 12,12 on a session you actually ran.
